chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one of you who belches the most in the world, he will be the one who hungers the most in the Hereafter' or he said: 'on the Day of Judgment'.

key_terms.أَبُو ذَرٍّ: Abu Dharr, a companion of the Prophet known for his piety
key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter, the life to come
key_terms.جُشَاءً: Belching or burping, indicating fullness or overeating

ai.seo_question: What is the connection between eating habits in this world and hunger in the afterlife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on the abhorrence of abundant eating, this narration from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari highlights the spiritual consequence of gluttony, linking physical satiety in the dunya to prolonged hunger on the Day of Judgment. In Shia tradition, this serves as a practical guideline for tazkiyah (purification of the self), emphasizing that moderation in consumption is essential to prevent the soul from becoming heavy with worldly attachments.
